I've mulled over this decision quite a bit, but I feel like this could work to give /v/Games its own identity. At the moment, we're little better than a "/v/Gaming with a filter". I don't feel that's worth splitting subscribers between two different subverses.

I've decided to move /v/Games in a new direction. It's now about the parts of a game, rather than specific games, or game discussions.

Easter Eggs, analysis of a soundtrack, design documents. As long as it's a post about parts of a game, or one about how different parts work together, then it's fair game.

Please take a look at the submission guidelines in the sidebar. Trailers, broad discussions, and reviews are not for /v/Games. They should be posted in /v/Gaming instead.

PLEASE NOTE: I am not a tyrant. This is not set in stone, and I will absolutely take feedback on this. I just feel the subverse is lacking a purpose at the moment, and am trying something new to fix that.

Feel free to use this thread to voice your complaints, or ask questions.

I think a solution would be to replace the up/down voat buttons with "funny", "helpful", "spam", "troll", etc. So people have to effectively state what aspect of the comment they are voting on. And allow a user to select multiple.

The problem is that there's no cost associated with down voting. I wouldn't hold Slashdot up as a shining beacon, but their moderation system worked the way you described. Another important feature was how a limited number of mod points are assigned to users, based in part on their contribution history, so they have value - people are less likely piss away your mod points when they might be the only ones you'll see this week, and they expire if not used. Also it was impossible to simultaneously post in a thread and moderate at the same time.

I wouldn't suggest the exact solution would work here, but I think a key is to add some kind cost to down voting. Personally I'd prefer to see karma go away altogether and for down votes to not allow a comment to be hidden (not sure if that happens here).

I think Slashdot had a karma system but without a number. You had maybe five text strings, so you might see something like "Karma: excellent", and then additional upvotes are not in any way indicated. Also, certain positive upvote reasons wouldn't affect the invisible karma number. The "Funny" option was positive but gave no positive benefits to karma, which I suppose would hopefully discourage the people who litter a conversation with their "funny" one-liners. Overall probably best to simply have no visible indications of karma. If someone is being a complete arse then we can use the report button and let the mod for that sub remove the comments and/or that person if they feel it necessary.

The reward for a good conversation is in being part of it - not the little numbers that tick-up when you say something non-controversial or funny, or when karma farmers deliberately target subs were they know they can rack-up the karma by posting memes or some other shite.
